about: The five stops of the boxwork Marswalk, in the order Curiosity reached them. Written by hand from docs/SCIENCE_BRIEF.md. 'rmc' names the Curiosity waypoint used as the stop's position: the rover's recorded position on that sol, not the exact position of the rock. 'found' is one short line from the cited source. Fields ending in 'Ours' are the team's own suggestions, not NASA statements.

stops.name: Altadena
stops.found: First drill site of the boxwork (8 Jun 2025). Bedrock laced with white calcium sulfate veins.
tasksOurs: Photograph the white veins along the outcrop.
Sample the freshest veins you can find.

stops.name: Nodule site
stops.found: Pea-sized nodules on ridge walls and in hollows. NASA cannot yet explain where they form.
tasksOurs: Find nodules on a ridge wall.
Collect several nodules in small vials.
Note where each sits: wall, hollow or fracture.

stops.name: Panorama viewpoint
stops.summary: The wide view of the boxwork
stops.found: Where Curiosity took its boxwork panorama (26 Sep 2025). Ridges and sandy hollows below.
tasksOurs: Photograph the ridge network from above.
Choose which fracture to follow next.

stops.name: Monte Grande hollow
stops.summary: Drill site Valle de la Luna
stops.found: Drill site in a sandy hollow (Oct 2025). NASA reports carbonates in a hollow sample.
stops.sourceLabel: NASA Curiosity mission blog, sols 4709 to 4715
tasksOurs: Dig through the sand of the hollow.
Core the bedrock under the sand.
Photograph the hollow floor before you dig.

stops.name: Nevado Sajama ridge
stops.summary: Drill site on the ridge beside the hollow
stops.found: Drill site on the ridge beside the hollow, 2 m higher. NASA reports clays in a ridgetop sample.
stops.sourceLabel: NASA Curiosity mission blog, sols 4709 to 4715
tasksOurs: Core the ridgetop, 10 m from the hollow site.
Break a rock open for a fresh face.
